description: Triages the witness-block-agreement checker's hardest row (6 of 7 published figures absent from the single witness declaring prop:em-coupling-projection). The BLOCK IS CORRECT: every figure reproduces at the proton pin from alpha_em_form_comparison_probe.py, the producer the table names in its own prose, and the table's claim that all rows use the proton pin is accurate. The real finding is that the contentBlock pointer is on the wrong producer -- em_coupling_projection_probe.py claims the block and computes 1 of 7 rows, while the producer of the other 6 emits no witness at all, so the block's machine-readable provenance covers 14 percent of it. Two label defects in the claiming witness, numbers untouched: (a) q0Value and q0Anchor correctly say proton while three prose sites say 'muon-anchored'; (b) CODATA_ALPHA_INV holds 137.035999206, which is the Morel et al. 2020 Rb-87 recoil measurement cited under that name in sec:fine-structure-data, not a CODATA adjustment. Both are numerically inert (Rb-87 vs CODATA 2022 is 2.1e-10 relative against a 5e-3 tolerance), which is why they survived. Third finding, cross-block: q[9]_q[10]_q is published at 136.823209 (proton) here and 136.823219654 (RETIRED vintage) in prop:em-coupling-bring-zero-mode, so two blocks disagree on one quantity in the 11th digit.
caveats: Says nothing about whether the Chern-Simons dressing is the right model of alpha_EM. rem:em-coupling-chern-simons is open, kappa is still a sorry, and the named producer's own output records that the smallest residual belongs to a RULED-OUT PSLQ-empirical form -- the signature of a fit, not evidence for one.
Says nothing about which pin either block SHOULD take. That is the owner ruling qou-i229 holds. No published figure is changed here.
